content_units: Auckland Move-Out Overview

This is a practical   tenant move-out checklist   for a residential apartment in   Auckland, New Zealand   with a fixed-term tenancy ending on   2026-02-28  . It is   general information, not legal advice  .
Timing note

Because   2026-02-28   falls at the end of the fixed term, plan to have the apartment empty, cleaned, documented, and keys ready to return   by the agreed handover time on that date   unless you and the landlord/property manager agree otherwise in writing.
Move-Out Timeline Checklist
Phase   Goal   Key Tasks   Deliverable

2-4 weeks before   Prepare exit plan   Check tenancy agreement; review inspection report from move-in; book cleaners if needed; arrange movers; confirm final day/time for handover   Written move-out plan

10-14 days before   Organise accounts and repairs   Give any required notice if applicable; schedule electricity/internet final readings or closure; replace blown bulbs; fix minor tenant-caused damage if appropriate   Utility end dates and repair list

3-7 days before   Deep clean and sort documents   Clean kitchen, bathroom, floors, windows accessible from inside, cupboards, appliances; remove rubbish; gather rent records and bond details   Apartment ready for final photos

Final day   Handover and evidence   Take timestamped photos/video of every room; photograph meters if relevant; attend inspection if offered; return all keys, fobs, remotes, parking cards   Handover evidence set
Within 1-3 days after   Finalise money and records   Complete bond refund process; confirm forwarding address; keep copies of all forms, emails, and receipts   Bond claim pack

Following weeks   Close out any disputes   Monitor bond status; respond promptly to landlord/property manager queries; keep all evidence until bond is refunded and issues are closed   Archived tenancy file
Apartment Move-Out Checklist
Cleaning standard to aim for
Leave the apartment   reasonably clean and tidy  , with all personal belongings removed.
- Kitchen:
- Clean oven, stovetop, rangehood filter surface, splashback, sink, taps, bench, cupboards, and fridge/freezer if included
- Remove food, grease, and rubbish
- Bathroom:
- Clean shower, toilet, vanity, mirrors, extractor cover surface, and visible mould/grime
- Living areas and bedrooms:
- Vacuum and mop floors as appropriate
- Wipe skirting boards, shelves, window sills, and wardrobe interiors
- Windows and surfaces:
- Clean internal glass where accessible
- Remove obvious marks from walls if safe to do so
- Balcony/storage:
- Remove rubbish and sweep
- Included items:
- Clean any landlord-provided appliances, curtains/blinds surfaces, heater filters if user-cleanable
Documentation to gather before leaving
- Copy of tenancy agreement
- Move-in inspection report and photos
- Latest rent ledger or payment proof
- Bond receipt/reference details
- Emails/texts with landlord or property manager
- Receipts for any professional cleaning, rubbish removal, or repairs
- Final utility bills or account closure confirmations
Photos and video to take on move-out day
Take clear, well-lit, timestamped images/video of:
- Each room from multiple angles
- Inside oven, fridge, cupboards, wardrobes
- Bathroom fixtures and shower
- Floor condition, carpet condition, and any pre-existing wear
- Windows, blinds/curtains, balcony, entry door
- Keys, remotes, fobs laid out before return
- Meter readings if relevant for power/gas/water
Key return and handover
- Return   all   keys, access fobs, mailbox keys, garage remotes, and parking/access cards
- Use the agreed return method: office handover, lockbox, or documented drop-off
- Ask for written confirmation that keys were returned, including date and time
- Keep a photo of the returned key set and any receipt/message confirming handover
Bond refund steps
- Confirm the property condition and any agreed deductions
- Complete the   bond refund   paperwork/process promptly after move-out
- Make sure your forwarding address, email, and bank details are correct
- Keep a signed copy or screenshot of the submission
- If there is disagreement, keep all evidence organised for follow-up
Utility and service closure
- Electricity: arrange final reading/end date
- Gas: arrange final reading/end date if applicable
- Internet: cancel or transfer service; return modem if required
- Water: check whether you pay directly and close/update if needed
- Contents insurance: cancel or update address
- NZ Post/mail: redirect mail and update address with bank, employer, subscriptions, and government agencies
Common Move-Out Disputes to Prepare For
The most common disagreements are usually about   cleaning, damage vs fair wear and tear, missing items, rent arrears, and key return timing  .
Issues tenants often get challenged on
-   Cleaning quality
Landlords/property managers may say the oven, bathroom, carpets, or cupboards were not cleaned well enough.
-   Damage claims
Scratches, stains, chipped paint, broken fittings, or cracked glass may be raised as tenant-caused damage.
-   Wear and tear disagreements
Normal aging can be confused with damage, especially for carpet flattening, minor scuffs, faded paint, and older appliances.
-   Missing chattels
Remote controls, curtains, shelves, smoke alarm parts, or appliance trays can become dispute points.
-   Outstanding charges
Unpaid rent, water, body corporate move-related charges, or cleaning invoices may be claimed.
-   Late vacancy or late key return
If keys are returned late, there may be arguments about extra rent/occupation liability.
Best ways to protect yourself
- Compare move-out photos directly against move-in photos
- Communicate in writing, not only by phone
- Attend the final inspection if possible
- Get receipts for cleaning/repairs
- Record exactly when possession was given back
- Keep all evidence until the bond is fully refunded and any dispute window has passed
Records to Keep After You Leave
Keep a digital folder and backup with:
- Signed tenancy agreement
- Bond confirmation and refund documents
- Rent payment history
- Entry and exit inspection reports
- Move-in and move-out photos/videos
- Utility closure confirmations
- Cleaning and repair receipts
- Key return proof
- All important emails, texts, and letters
A good rule is to keep these records until the   bond is refunded and all tenancy issues are fully resolved  , and longer if any dispute is ongoing.
